Strategic Acquisitions & Roll-ups in India

A strategic acquisition adds capabilities to an existing business. A roll-up combines multiple businesses around an operating platform. Both require disciplined target selection and a realistic integration plan, not just access to capital.

Start a private enquiry ↗

Choose the platform thesis

Define the repeatable advantage: distribution, procurement, shared infrastructure, technology, geographic density or management systems. If the advantage cannot be explained without assuming a higher exit multiple, the thesis needs more work.

Evaluate each acquisition independently

Review each target’s standalone economics, integration demands, customer relationships and management depth. Compare acquisition cost with organic alternatives. Avoid assuming that small companies are automatically cheap or easy to integrate.

Design integration before signing

Clarify which functions will remain local and which will be centralised. Assign responsibility for customer retention, key staff, systems, reporting and synergy delivery. Sequence acquisitions according to operational capacity.

How Legacy Search can help

We help corporate buyers define acquisition criteria, identify potential businesses and coordinate conversations. We can support a single strategic acquisition or a repeatable origination mandate, subject to agreed scope and fit.

Common questions

What is the difference between a platform and an add-on?

A platform is the operating foundation; an add-on complements its capabilities, coverage or scale.

Are roll-ups appropriate in every sector?

No. Fragmentation alone is insufficient. Integration economics, demand, regulation and operational capacity matter.
